headline: Medium risk: shared MCP and file-based workflows create prompt-injection and data-flow exposure, while ComfyUI’s offline defaults limit severity.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman uses MCP and file surfaces like CLAUDE.md/project notes, so it can ingest external content as instructions; ComfyUI is a separate image workflow tool, but if its outputs are copied into caveman or a shared MCP channel exists, injection is plausible. No direct bridge is documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF caveman reads ComfyUI-generated text from a shared file or MCP channel, prompt injection becomes active.
IF an operator pastes ComfyUI output into caveman without sanitization, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP server between the tools.
Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate folder from caveman inputs.
Paste only structured, non-executable summaries into caveman.
Add a one-line provenance tag to copied outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering on the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes, while ComfyUI touches images, workflows, and model artifacts. Both are open-source and ComfyUI can run fully offline, so the main leakage path is a shared workspace rather than automatic third-party exfiltration. That makes the blast radius limited and the pathway configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace directory, files may be exposed across tools.
IF sensitive images are placed in caveman-readable notes, they can be surfaced in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for notes and image assets.
Remove secrets from project notes before sharing them.
Set read permissions so caveman cannot access image folders.
Keep ComfyUI offline when handling sensitive media.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses files/MCP, while ComfyUI does not write filesystems or modify git state and lacks shell execution. Overlapping write capability is therefore not evident; the main conflict is limited to coordination around shared artifacts, which is a small blast radius compared with true concurrent mutation.
conditions: IF both tools are pointed at the same mutable directory, artifact races can occur.
IF an operator manually edits the same workflow file in both tools, last-write-wins conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign each tool its own working directory.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same workflow file.
Use read-only mounts for shared reference assets.
Serialize manual changes through one operator.
requires-engineering: add file locking for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can generate project notes and instructions that ComfyUI may consume as workflow inputs, and ComfyUI can then render outputs based on those inputs. There is no documented verification loop between them, so mistaken or malicious text can cascade into incorrect images or workflows. The pathway is inferred from their file/API surfaces, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF ComfyUI consumes caveman-authored prompts or workflow JSON without review, errors propagate downstream.
IF caveman summarizes ComfyUI outputs as facts, later actions may be based on those summaries.
mitigations: Require human review before ComfyUI runs a caveman-generated workflow.
Keep source prompts and rendered outputs in separate folders.
Mark caveman summaries as untrusted until verified.
Use a checklist for prompt-to-workflow translation.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for workflow inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no requested secrets or special certifications, so there is no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch documented. The only plausible compliance issue is handling sensitive project notes or images in shared storage, which is a limited, operator-controlled gap rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in shared notes or image folders, retention and access controls must be enforced.
IF the deployment adds a third-party backend for either tool, residency obligations may change.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Document retention rules for notes and images.
Confirm any added backend’s region before use.
Delete temporary artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
